spatial_entity.notes: Bounded Qin imperial slice chosen to match evidence and available Cliopatria time slices.

claim.summary: Qin convict labour formed a complex state-administered system that coerced legally degraded men, women and children into work for state projects. Excavated statutes and administrative records show penal labour as a routine punishment and a major labour source; Liye evidence from newly conquered Qianling documents the management of laborer-servants through supervision and punishment.

territorial_practice.notes: P3 reflects an institutional state convict-labour regime. Evidence from exceptionally well-documented Qianling is not mechanically generalized into a population estimate for the entire Qin Empire.

source.title: From the “Empire of Convicts” to Labor Market: Convict Labor Regime in the Early Chinese Empires and Its Legacy
source.independence_notes: Recent specialist synthesis centered on excavated Qin and Han legal/administrative documents.
source.reliability_limitations: Qianling is exceptionally well documented; its local demographic proportions should not be generalized empire-wide.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist interpretation of Qin convict-labour regime
evidence.directness: specialist synthesis of excavated legal and administrative texts
evidence.locator: Abstract and section 'Convict-Labor Institutions in Qin and Early-Western Han'

source.title: Categorizing Laborers: Glimpses of Qin Management of Human Resources from an Administrative Document from Liye, Hunan Province
source.independence_notes: Contextual study of a Liye multi-slip administrative manuscript with related Qin excavated sources.
source.reliability_limitations: The focal manuscript concerns Qianling County and does not by itself quantify the whole Qin Empire.
